requirements.text: Trip creation supports a start/end date range, including single-day and same-start/end-day trips, with correct day math.
Each trip has multiple days, each with an ordered list of stops.
Stop model includes place name, address, optional MapKit-resolved coordinate, time window, notes, and category icon.
Stops can be reordered via drag-and-drop within a day.
Stops can be reordered via drag-and-drop across days, implemented as a single atomic SwiftData operation with no orphaned or duplicated stops at any intermediate state.
A non-gesture 'Move to...' action exists alongside drag-and-drop, routed through the identical atomic operation, for accessibility.
A moved stop's time window is preserved on cross-day move and visually flagged if it falls outside the new day's typical range.
A per-day MapKit view shows all of that day's stops as annotations connected by a route line.
Routing uses MKDirections walking/driving when resolvable, gracefully degrading to a straight-line polyline with a visible 'approximate' indicator when unavailable.
Tapping a stop centers the map and highlights it; tapping a map pin selects the corresponding itinerary row (two-way binding).
A per-trip list of travelers (name only, no accounts) can be created and managed.
Expenses can be logged with amount, payer, split method (equal/exact/percentage), and any subset of travelers.
All money values use Decimal, never Double, throughout the app.
Percentage splits that do not sum to 100% are rejected at entry with an inline error stating the actual sum; the app never silently auto-rescales.
A settle-up screen computes the mathematically minimal set of payments (debt-simplification) to zero every balance.
Rounding remainder cents are deterministically assigned to the expense's payer, with an in-code sum-identity assertion that shares sum exactly to the original Decimal amount.
Settlement correctness is validated adversarially: 4+ travelers, a payer excluded from their own expense's split, and rejected non-100%-summing percentages.
Cross-day drag integrity is validated with 10+ rapid repeated moves of one stop across 3+ days with no duplication/loss observable at any intermediate state.
Editing a trip's date range to a shorter span that would orphan stops on removed days blocks the edit and shows exactly which days/stops are affected; extending the range is unrestricted.
A per-trip packing checklist exists with a packed-percentage indicator that recalculates correctly as items change.
Packing templates can be saved and reapplied to future trips.
While a trip is active (today within its date range), a Live Activity/Dynamic Island shows the current or next stop and time until it, updating as stops are checked off.
Live Activity degrades gracefully (no crash, no Live Activity) on unsupported devices/OS versions and when the user denies the permission.
Live Activity updates are local/scheduled-only; no push-token or server-driven update mechanism is used.
A day's stops can be exported as EventKit calendar events (one event per stop, honoring its time window) with explicit user permission.
Calendar export is idempotent: the EventKit event identifier is stored per stop at export time; re-export looks it up and updates the existing event in place rather than duplicating.
Calendar export handles an externally-deleted event or revoked Calendar permission as an explicit, non-crashing, non-lying state.
A home-screen widget (separate WidgetKit target) shows the active trip's next stop, or an honest 'no active trip' state if none.

On iPad, the itinerary list and map work as a genuine two-column split view (independently interactive panes), not a stretched phone layout, verified across at least two iPad sizes and both orientations.
Every permission/capability-gated feature (Live Activity, Calendar, MapKit routing without network, location if used) has an observed — not just coded — correct denied/unavailable state.
A demo trip Settings toggle is a singleton keyed by a stable identifier: toggling on creates it only if absent, toggling off deletes exactly that trip and never touches real trips.
The demo trip and its data carry a visible 'Demo' marker wherever they appear, including widget and Live Activity surfaces.
The demo trip includes at least one stop that deliberately fails MKDirections route resolution, so the approximate-route fallback is actually observed.
A new user's first launch (demo toggle off) shows genuine, honest empty states everywhere, with zero fabricated content.
All stop times are stored and displayed in the device's current local timezone; destination-timezone-aware itineraries are out of scope and named in Gaps.
CloudKit/iCloud sync for SwiftData is disabled by default and not silently scaffolded on.
No backend, no accounts, no third-party SDKs, and no network calls except on-device MapKit/local geocoding.
The debug current-date injection hook used for testing 'is trip active' logic is wrapped in #if DEBUG and physically excluded from release builds.
A Gaps section explicitly names: live traffic data, real-time flight tracking, iCloud trip sync, and destination-timezone-aware itineraries as out of scope.
Every screen has designed empty, loading, success, and error states where reachable, with no default unstyled List/Form where the design calls for custom rows.
The app fully supports dark mode with semantic color roles verified in both appearances.
The app is runnable in the iOS Simulator via Xcode with clear run instructions.

A StoreKit Pro tier (annual subscription + lifetime purchase in one product group) gates unlimited trips, packing templates, calendar export, Live Activity, widget, and audit-log reporting behind a single active-trip-count gate, while settlement math, iPad split view, and honest map-degradation are never paywalled.
A lapsed subscription or failed restore never deletes, hides, or corrupts existing trip data; it only locks new-trip creation past the free cap and Pro-only surfaces.
A one-way, explicitly labeled 'Trip Snapshot' export (PDF/text/.ics) defaults to itinerary-only content, excluding expense/settlement data unless the owner opts in.
A settlement audit-log/category-spend-breakdown report is available as a Pro reporting layer on top of already-correct free settlement math.
